                                 STATEMENT OF THE CASE

1.     Under the Public Utility Regulatory Act (PURA), an electric utility must obtain a

certificate of convenience and necessity (CCN) from the Public Utility Commission of Texas

(PUC or Commission) to install, operate, or extend electric utility service to the public.

2.     To approve an application to obtain or amend a CCN, the PUC must find the proposed

CCN is “necessary for the service, accommodation, convenience, or safety of the public.” Texas

statutes and PUC rules set forth the criteria according to which the PUC makes it decisions and

includes factors that the Commission must consider when approving and/or choosing a new

transmission line.

3.     Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC (Oncor) and LCRA Transmission Services

Corporation (LCRA) filed a joint application to amend its CCN for the Bell County East Switch

to Big Hill Substation 765 kV Transmission Line Project on March 26, 2026.

4.     From June 8, 2026 through June 12, 2026, the SOAH administrative law judges (ALJs)

held a hearing on the merits of applicants’ amended application.

5.     The ALJs will prepare a proposal for decision (PFD) that analyzes the evidence and

makes recommendations to the Commission regarding this proposed transmission line. The

ALJ’s have the authority to deny the application in its entirety after reviewing the evidence and

applying the law. The Commission must accept the PFD, modify it, or deny the amended

application.
                                         I.      INTRODUCTION

teachers, churches, municipalities, counties, and more than 800 other intervenors that have

provided evidence in this case – to deny the Bell County to Big Hill 765 kV line joint application

in its entirety.

12.     In short, the need for the transmission line is hotly debated and not clearly established;

the line will negatively impact the health of children and families in Texas as never before; it

will devalue Texas landowners’ property as never before; it will damage Texas gas pipelines as

never before; and it will irreparably damage Texas parks and wildlife as never before in the

history of our great state. The seriousness of these issues and the ensuing damages to our state

are unprecedented in any PUC case that has come before the Commission, SOAH and the public.

             I.     WHY APPLICATION SHOULD BE DENIED IN ITS ENTIRETY

          A. Application Fails to Meet PUC’s Order of Referral and Preliminary Order
                       Need for This Transmission Line Not Established

Oncor and LCRA’s Application address specific and critical “Need” issues and metrics - and

they have not:

         Need - 5.a. How do the proposed transmission facilities support the reliability and
          adequacy of the interconnected transmission system?8
         Need – 7.a. The data used to calculate the applicant's load-growth projections that
          support the need for a transmission-line solution.9

14.       In Oncor and LCRA’s joint amended application Exhibit 1, there is no information

regarding how much power the Bell County to Big Hill 765 kV transmission line will transfer to

the Permian Basin. There is zero information of the expected power the line will transfer “to

support the reliability and adequacy of the interconnected transmission system.”10

15.       Oncor and LCRA’s Exhibit 1, their amended Application, is completely silent and devoid

of the data required to document how much power transmission the Bell County to Big Hill 765

kV power line is committing to transfer to the Permian Basis and how that amount of power

transfer addresses the reliability plan.

16.       At the Hearing on the Merits, on June 9, 2026, Dr. Pressley specifically asked PUC
